findings.reason: the plan's own node write path includes `documents/pipeline.py` specifically to make this deletion, so the author must either extend `base/image.py` with the claim-aware predicate or drop the deletion; as written it silently changes document-discovery behaviour under the banner of removing a duplicate.
findings.text: the plan deletes `_has_pending_image_scores` claiming it "duplicates the public `has_pending_image_work`" (`imas_codex/discovery/base/image.py:354`), but the two predicates are not duplicates: `_has_pending_image_scores` selects `img.status = 'ingested' AND img.claimed_at IS NULL`, while `has_pending_image_work` selects `img.status = 'ingested' AND img.description IS NULL`; they can and will disagree (a claimed image mid-scoring, or an unclaimed image that already has a description), so deleting the pipeline one and calling the image one changes which images the document pipeline reports as pending — and the deeper difference is that `has_pending_image_work` swallows exceptions returning `False` where the pipeline helper does not; the owner to extend is `imas_codex/discovery/base/image.py`, which should gain the claim-aware predicate (or the plan should keep the pipeline predicate and state the difference) rather than the plan asserting a duplicate that does not exist

findings.reason: the registry's finer stage list is legitimately more granular than the domain list, so a divergence is expected, but the plan's claim that its domains *are* `DISCOVERY_DOMAINS` is inaccurate and should be corrected to "derived from" so a later domain addition does not leave one list stale.
findings.text: the same "one set, two owners" defect recurs one level up: `DISCOVERY_DOMAINS = ("paths","wiki","signals","code","documents","map")` already owns the domain enumeration, and §2's registry introduces a second, finer nine-stage enumeration ("Its domains are the existing `DISCOVERY_DOMAINS`") whose stages (signals scan/enrich/check, candidates, mapping) do not map one-to-one onto those six domains, so the two enumerations overlap without either deriving from the other and will drift when a domain is added; the owner to extend is `DISCOVERY_DOMAINS` in `common.py` (or the registry should declare a mapping onto it)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `imas_codex/cli/discover/sequence.py` hides ordering, access probing, budget partitioning and per-stage fault isolation behind the single `discover run FACILITY` command; the stage metadata is a data registry (a table), not a spread of small wrappers over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's dedup target is wrong, and it would leave two enumerations of one domain set.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 names the added surface (`discover run` plus five options) and states nothing is retired and why the per-domain commands and their stage-specific options cannot be collapsed into the sequence ("the per-domain commands stay the way to run one stage with its stage-specific options, for example `discover signals --category`, which the sequence does not re-declare").
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase it extends and cites it with line numbers I verified against the source: `DISCOVERY_DOMAINS` (`imas_codex/cli/discover/common.py:30`), `run_discovery` (`common.py:212`), `ensure_remote_environment` (`common.py:443`), `create_discovery_monitor` (`common.py:502`), the three check functions (`imas_codex/discovery/base/services.py:159,178,200`), the per-domain `has_pending_*` predicates, and `discover_mappable_ids` (`imas_codex/ids/tools.py:376`); no existing cross-domain sequencing command exists, so the orchestrator is genuinely new and not a missed reuse.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the `ctx.invoke` runner is a thin layer, and the plan states in its own text why the existing commands cannot be folded into it instead: invoking each stage's click command is "the only path that reuses each stage whole, without refactoring seven commands or starting subprocesses" (§3).
